objective: Predict known SV class (INS/DEL/INV) from frozen first-affected-base reference-segment representations, controlling chromosome/length-bin distributions.
probe: Separate native balanced logistic C=1 one-versus-rest probe for each class; frozen v1 T and NT S. Native train-only scaling, validation-only temperature/F1 threshold. No tuning on test.
partition: All five original chromosome folds, three checkpoint seeds and both contexts; every event and repeated anchor remains chromosome grouped.
matching: Fixed chromosome and length bins, equal class counts without replacement, seed 20260927, hash-ordered IDs. 223 events per class, 669 total. 75 primary-chromosome inversions outside common support are retained in natural_events.parquet.
representation: One BED first-affected-base anchor per event for every class. No END/distance/ID/donor metadata in C/S/T. Event log length is explicitly labeled L and evaluated separately.
inference: Per-class one-versus-rest AP plus macro average over all three classes; paired hierarchical fold/seed bootstrap, exact fold sign-flip and BH within metric over all classes/macro, contexts and contrasts. Macro binary metrics are not joint multiclass accuracy.
validity_gates: Complete C/S/T/H coverage and exact source/checkpoint identities
Same test event identities in every arm/class
No bin changes based on performance
limitations: Common-support matched population, not natural class prevalence or all 298 inversions
Known-SV type classification, not discovery, pathogenicity, or breakpoint detection
New anchor representation differs from original two-breakpoint INS/DEL benchmark
No DUP/complex labels in these input tables; no class relabeling
Graph donor overlap and v1 shortcut caveats remain
Static reference-segment vectors cannot distinguish events with identical features; no learned-versus-random claim
